# Adjudication Task — Chapter 493

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃493화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|기회는 모든 사람에게 공평하게 주어지지 않는다.
  6|
  7|그런 의미에서 보자면 불과 열 살의 나이로 무당파 장문인의 적전 제자가 된 현공진인(玄空眞人)은 다른 이들에 비해 많은 기회를 얻은 인물이라 할 수 있었다.
  8|
  9|그야말로 탄탄대로.
 10|
 11|당대에 손꼽히는 무재를 타고난 데다 성정도 올곧은 현공진인은 늘 전폭적인 지원을 받았다.
 12|
 13|그것은 반대로 말하자면, 그가 일평생 부족함을 느껴본 적이 없다는 뜻이기도 했다.
 14|
 15|하지만…….
 16|
 17|‘갖고 싶다.’
 18|
 19|현공진인의 눈동자가 잘게 흔들렸다. 그건 실로 오랜만에 느끼는 물질적인 욕망이었다.
 20|
 21|‘이런 적이 없었거늘.’
 22|
 23|황금과 부귀영화? 그런 것 따위는 필요 없었다.
 24|
 25|한번 받은 도포는 닳아 없어질 때까지 입었고 늘 정갈하고 단출한 식사로 끼니를 때웠다.
 26|
 27|영약, 비급도 마찬가지다. 초절정의 경지에 오른 뒤부터는 정신 수양에 힘썼던 그다.
 28|
 29|장문 사형이 영약을 권해도 앞길 창창한 귀여운 사손들에게 양보했고, 비급은 지금까지 익힌 무당파의 절기로도 차고 넘쳤다.
 30|
 31|하지만, 하지만 이건.
 32|
 33|“후우, 무량수불. 무량수불.”
 34|
 35|현공진인은 거칠게 자신의 수염을 쓸어내리며 법문을 외웠다.
 36|
 37|그러나 애써 다스리려는 마음과는 달리 눈길은 자꾸만 이무기의 사체를 향하고 있었다.
 38|
 39|‘저게 그렇게 단단하다던데.’
 40|
 41|갈라진 비늘과 쩍 벌어진 상흔(傷痕) 사이로, 은은한 빛을 뿌리는 거대한 뼈가 보인다.
 42|
 43|오백 년 묵은 이무기라 그런지 때깔부터 다른 저 뼈는, 어지간한 검기로도 베어 내지 못할 만큼의 강도를 자랑한다고 들었다.
 44|
 45|‘만약 저 뼈로 검을 만든다면 기가 막힐…… 아니, 아니다. 지금 무슨 생각을 하는 것이냐. 현공아!’
 46|
 47|현공진인은 눈을 질끈 감았다. 태원진가의 두 형제에 의해 제갈풍이 너덜너덜해진 꼴을 목격한 직후라 더더욱 그랬다.
 48|
 49|그나마 제갈풍은 전투가 벌어질 때 함께 있기라도 했지, 그는 수백 리 떨어진 동정채의 본거지에 있었다.
 50|
 51|현공진인에게는 무언가를 요구할 만한 명분도, 부끄러움을 무릅쓰고 부탁할 만한 염치도 없었다.
 52|
 53|‘무량수불, 무량수불. 도사씩이나 되어 이런 삿된 욕망에 정신을 빼앗기다니. 정신 차리거라, 현공아.’
 54|
 55|현공진인이 남몰래 속앓이만 하고 있던 바로 그때였다.
 56|
 57|“진인. 바쁘십니까?”
 58|
 59|“음?”
 60|
 61|현공진인은 감았던 눈을 번쩍 떴다. 낯익은 얼굴의 젊은이가 그를 은근한 시선으로 바라보고 있었다.
 62|
 63|‘진태경.’
 64|
 65|젊은이의 정체는 검성의 제자인 화산신룡 청풍과 함께 무림을 뒤흔들고 있는 돌풍의 주역이었다.
 66|
 67|떠들기 좋아하는 호사가들 사이에서는 이미 십왕(十王) 아래에 이룡(二龍)이 있다는 말까지 돌고 있을 정도다.
 68|
 69|‘대단한 젊은이지. 믿기 힘들 정도로.’
 70|
 71|하지만 지금 현공진인에게 중요한 것은 진태경에 대한 평가가 아니었다.
 72|
 73|‘혹시?’
 74|
 75|약간의 희망과 설렘. 노 도사는 두근거리는 마음을 안고 진태경을 바라보았다.
 76|
 77|“무슨 일인가. 진 도우?”
 78|
 79|진태경이 부드럽게 웃으며 대답했다.
 80|
 81|“바쁘시지 않다면 대화를 청해도 될까 싶어서요.”
 82|
 83|“대화라면, 어떤 용무인가.”
 84|
 85|“이제 사체를 처리해야 하는데, 생각보다 양이 많지 뭡니까.”
 86|
 87|“그, 그래서?”
 88|
 89|“다른 분도 아니고 현공진인께서 직접 여기까지 오셨는데, 당연히 얻어 가시는 게 있어야 하지 않겠습니까.”
 90|
 91|“허어!”
 92|
 93|대번에 초롱초롱해지는 현공진인의 눈동자. 그 모습에 빙긋 웃은 진태경이 재차 말을 이었다.
 94|
 95|“저희 태원진가는 늘 무당파의 도사님들을 존경해 온 바, 같은 무림 동도로서 기쁜 마음으로 이번 수확을 조금이나마 나누고자 합니다.”
 96|
 97|“그, 그것이 참말인가?”
 98|
 99|“어휴, 그럼요. 혁무진의 불알을 걸고 맹세합니다. 그리고 이건 제 큰형님께서도 적극 찬성한 사안입니다.”
100|
101|“세상에나, 무량수불!”
102|
103|차마 염치가 있어 부탁하지 못한 가려운 부분을 살살 긁어 주니, 현공진인은 기뻐서 어쩔 줄을 몰랐다.
104|
105|혁무진이 누구인지, 왜 그의 불알을 걸고 맹세하는지는 몰라도 일단 나눠 준다는 게 중요하다.
106|
107|‘이토록 선량할 수가!’
108|
109|말만 번지르르한 위선자들과는 격이 다르다.
110|
111|몰염치한 인간군상들이 득실거리는 이 차가운 무림에 내리쬔 한 줄기 빛.
112|
113|이제 현공진인은 진태경의 머리 위로 후광마저 보일 지경이었다.
114|
115|“참으로 고맙네! 원시천존께서 진 도우와 태원진가를 보우하시길! 무량수불!”
116|
117|“아멘.”
118|
119|뭔가 이상했지만 현공진인에게는 아무런 상관도 없었다.
120|
121|그리고 만면에 웃음을 가득 머금고 있던 그를 향해, 진태경의 부드러운 목소리가 이어졌다.
122|
123|“그런데 사소한 문제가 하나 있습니다.”
124|
125|“으응? 사소한 문제라니?”
126|
127|“아무래도 사체가 워낙에 크다 보니 저 혼자는 처리하기 벅차지 뭡니까. 그렇다고 이걸 통째로 옮길 수도 없고요.”
128|
129|“그렇지. 그렇고말고.”
130|
131|머리부터 꼬리까지, 장장 백여 장에 달하는 거체다.
132|
133|이런 걸 통째로 옮길 수 있는지도 의문이거니와, 그만한 인력이 투입될 테니 기밀 유지는 더더욱 불가능했다.
134|
135|“해서 진인께 작은 부탁을 하나 드리고자 합니다.”
136|
137|순간 멈칫한 현공진인의 눈동자에 의혹의 빛이 스쳤다.
138|
139|“잠깐. 진 도우. 그 부탁이라는 게 혹시……?”
140|
141|“예. 힘 좀 써 주셔야겠습니다. 이대로 가다가는 며칠씩 걸리겠어요.”
142|
143|이거였구나! 호의를 베푼 이유가!
144|
145|현공진인은 배신당한 표정으로 진태경을 노려보았다.
146|
147|“그러니까 지금, 저 이무기의 사체를 분리하는 것에 무당파의 검공을 사용하라는 말인가?”
148|
149|“쉽게 생각하시면 됩니다. 작업이죠.”
150|
151|“쉽게 생각하라니, 작업이라니! 빈도는 이런 일을 위해 무공을 수련한 것이 아닐세!”
152|
153|누군가 초절정의 경지에 올랐다는 것은 그의 인생 대부분을, 아니 인생 전부를 무공에 바쳤다는 뜻이다.
154|
155|현공진인 역시 마찬가지였다. 한 자루 검을 벗 삼아, 정인 삼아 보낸 세월이 몇 년인가.
156|
157|컴컴한 어둠 속에서 면벽수련(面壁修練)까지 해 가며 무공을 갈고 닦았던 그에게 있어 진태경의 부탁은 모욕이나 다름없었다.
158|
159|‘괘씸한지고.’
160|
161|현공진인은 딱딱하게 굳은 얼굴로 입을 열었다.
162|
163|“무량수불. 진 도우. 자네는 지금 빈도는 물론이고 대무당파의 검공을 욕보인 걸세.”
164|
165|“욕을 보이다니, 그럴 리가 있겠습니까. 그저 한 손 거들어 주십사 청하는 것뿐입니다.”
166|
167|“하지만 빈도의 검을 고작 이런 일에 쓸 수는 없…….”
168|
169|현공진인의 목소리가 높아지려던 그 순간, 진태경이 불쑥 한마디를 툭 던졌다.
170|
171|“지금 보니 검이 상당히 낡았네요.”
172|
173|“뭣이?”
174|
175|“슬슬 바꾸실 때가 된 것 같은데. 어떻게 생각하십니까?”
176|
177|“……!”
178|
179|현공진인의 동공이 지진이라도 난 것처럼 흔들렸다.
180|
181|자신도 모르게 허리춤에 매인 낡은 송문고검을 바라본 그의 뇌리에 문득 한 가지 생각이 스쳤다.
182|
183|‘확실히 낡긴 했…… 아니, 지금 내가 무슨 생각을!’
184|
185|열 살 때부터 늘 몸에 지니고 있던 검이다. 돌아가신 스승님께 받은 귀중한 물건이기도 했다.
186|
187|황급히 고개를 흔들어 정신을 차린 현공진인이 눈을 부릅떴다.
188|
189|“안 낡았네!”
190|
191|“낡았습니다. 직접 보세요. 우선 검파(劍把)만 봐도 완전 너덜거리는데.”
192|
193|“그런 것 같기도 하…… 아닐세! 잘못 본 게야!”
194|
195|“그럼 그건 그렇다 치고, 검갑에도 금이 잔뜩 갔는데요. 가뭄 들었습니까?”
196|
197|“아앗. 이건 또 언제…….”
198|
199|“아, 이거 상태가 심각하네. 검 좀 뽑아 보시겠어요?”
200|
201|“빈도가 왜 그래야 하나!”
202|
203|스릉!
204|
205|호통을 친 현공진인은 뒤늦게 자신이 검을 뽑았다는 사실을 알고 경악했다.
206|
207|‘도대체 언제!’
208|
209|하지만 그러거나 말거나, 마귀의 속삭임은 계속되고 있었다.
210|
211|“검신도 영 상태가 좋지 못한데요.”
212|
213|“작고하신 스승님께서 주신 물건일세!”
214|
215|진태경이 태연한 표정으로 대꾸했다.
216|
217|“제 몸도 부모님께서 주셨는데, 쓰다 보니 망가지더라고요. 바꿀 수만 있었으면 진작 바꿨을 겁니다.”
218|
219|“하긴 빈도도 요즘 삭신이 쑤셔서 환골탈태(換骨奪胎)가 마려울 지경…… 지금 뭐 하자는 겐가!”
220|
221|“뭐 하긴요. 냉정한 현실을 알려 드리는 겁니다. 오, 날 부분은 아직 예리한데요?”
222|
223|정신 차리자. 정신 차려야 한다, 현공아.
224|
225|호흡으로 흐트러지는 정신을 가다듬은 현공진인이 자부심 넘치는 목소리로 대답했다.
226|
227|“당연하지. 다른 것도 아닌 만년한철을 넉 냥이나 섞어 검날을 벼렸으니까.”
228|
229|“세상에. 그 귀하다는 만년한철을 넉 냥이나요?”
230|
231|“이제 알겠나? 이 검이 보기에는 낡았을지 몰라도 보검(寶劍)이라 불리기에 조금도 부족함이 없다는 것을.”
232|
233|“아하. 그렇습니까?”
234|
235|“물론일세! 이미 누구나 탐낼 만큼 좋은 검을 가졌는데 뭣 하러 다른 검을…….”
236|
237|철컹!
238|
239|“아, 죄송합니다. 손이 미끄러워서 그런지 창을 떨어트렸네요. 말씀 계속하세요.”
240|
241|머쓱하게 웃는 진태경의 얼굴은 눈에 들어오지도 않는다.
242|
243|은은한 빛을 뿌리는 한 자루의 창을 바라보는 현공진인의 눈꺼풀이 파르르 떨렸다.
244|
245|“지, 진 도우. 그거 설마…….”
246|
247|“별거 아닙니다. 이것도 만년한철로 만든 건데, 진인께서 갖고 계시는 검에 비하면 아무것도 아니죠.”
248|
249|전혀 안 그래 보이는데.
250|
251|마른침을 꿀꺽 삼킨 현공진인이 조심스럽게 물었다.
252|
253|“혹시…… 몇 냥?”
254|
255|“통짜. 날부터 창대까지 전부.”
256|
257|“이런 미친. 무량수불.”
258|
259|“예? 뭐라고요?”
260|
261|“아, 아닐세. 아무것도.”
262|
263|마귀다. 이건 마귀의 속삭임이다.
264|
265|하지만 홀린 듯이 법문을 외는 현공진인의 시선은 진태경의 창, 백염(白炎)에 고정되어 있었다.
266|
267|“가볍기는 깃털 같고, 단단하기는 또 얼마나 단단합니까. 심지어 예리하기까지 해요. 그런데.”
268|
269|이어 노 도사의 귓가를 파고드는 나긋나긋한 유혹의 음성.
270|
271|“저는 이무기의 뼈로 만든 병장기가 갖고 싶더라고요.”
272|
273|“무량수불. 나는 아닐세.”
274|
275|“잘 생각해 보십시오. 다른 것도 아니고 자그마치 오백 년이나 살아온 신령스러운 이무기의 기운이 고스란히 깃들어 있는 병장기라면?”
276|
277|당연히 끝내주겠지. 진짜 갖고 싶다.
278|
279|치미는 말을 간신히 삼킨 현공진인이 미친 듯이 고개를 흔들었다.
280|
281|“불가! 빈도는 결코 스승님께서 주신 검을 버릴 수 없…….”
282|
283|“누가 그 소중한 걸 버립니까. 둘 다 가지면 되는 거죠.”
284|
285|“이런 씨발 그런 방법이! 아아 원시천존이시여!”

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). **Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

Elixirs and martial arts manuals were no different. Since reaching the Supreme Peak realm, he had devoted himself to cultivating his mind. Whenever his Senior Brother, the Sect Leader, offered him an elixir, Hyeongong passed it on to his promising grand-disciples. As for manuals, the Wudang techniques he had already mastered were more than enough.

[P12]
But this. This was different.

[P13]
“Hoo… Infinite Life Buddha. Infinite Life Buddha.”

[P14]
Hyeongong ran a rough hand down his beard and recited the invocation. Yet despite his efforts to master himself, his gaze kept returning to the imugi’s corpse.

[P15]
*They say those bones are incredibly hard.*

[P16]
Enormous bones glowed faintly between the split scales and gaping wounds. Perhaps five hundred years inside an imugi had given them that extraordinary luster. He had heard that ordinary Sword Energy could barely cut through them.

[P17]
*If I made a sword from those bones, it would be incredible… No. What am I thinking? Get a grip, Hyeongong!*

[P18]
He squeezed his eyes shut. He had just watched the two Jin brothers leave Zhuge Feng in tatters, which made the temptation all the more troubling.

[P19]
At least Zhuge Feng had been there when the battle took place. Hyeongong had been hundreds of li away, at the Donghu Stronghold headquarters. He had no grounds to demand anything, nor the nerve to set aside his shame and ask.

[P20]
*Infinite Life Buddha, Infinite Life Buddha. A Daoist, led astray by a desire like this? Get a hold of yourself, Hyeongong.*

[P21]
While he was struggling in silence, someone spoke.

[P22]
“Perfected Being. Are you busy?”

[P23]
“Hm?”

[P24]
Hyeongong’s eyes flew open. A familiar young man was watching him with a suggestive look.

[P25]
*Jin Taekyung.*

[P26]
Together with the Sword Saint’s Disciple, Cheongpung—the Huashan Divine Dragon—this young man was at the center of the storm sweeping through Murim. The gossips were already saying that beneath the Ten Kings stood the Two Dragons.

[P27]
*An extraordinary young man. Almost unbelievably so.*

[P28]
But Hyeongong had something more pressing on his mind than his opinion of Jin Taekyung.

[P29]
*Could it be?*

[P30]
The old Daoist looked at him, his heart quickening with hope.

[P31]
“What is it, young friend?”

[P32]
Taekyung smiled gently. “If you’re not busy, I was hoping we could talk.”

[P33]
“Talk? About what?”

[P34]
“We have to deal with the corpse now, and there’s more of it than we expected.”

[P35]
“Th-Then?”

[P36]
“You came all the way here in person. Of course you should have something to take home.”

[P37]
“Oh!”

[P38]
Hyeongong’s eyes lit up at once. Taekyung smiled and went on.

[P39]
“Our Jin Family of Taiyuan has always held the Daoists of Wudang in the highest regard. As fellow martial artists of Murim, we’d be delighted to share a little of what we’ve gained.”

[P40]
“I-Is that true?”

[P41]
“Of course. I swear on Hyuk Mujin’s balls. My eldest brother is fully in favor of it too.”

[P42]
“Good heavens! Infinite Life Buddha!”

[P43]
Taekyung had gently scratched the itch Hyeongong had been too ashamed to mention. The old Daoist was beside himself with joy.

[P44]
He had no idea who Hyuk Mujin was or why Taekyung was swearing on the man’s balls. What mattered was that Wudang would receive a share.

[P45]
*How can anyone be this kind?*

[P46]
Taekyung was nothing like the hypocrites with their fine words. He was a ray of light shining into a cold Murim crawling with shameless people.

[P47]
Hyeongong could practically see a halo over his head.

[P48]
“Thank you! May the Primordial Heavenly Venerable protect you and the Jin Family of Taiyuan, young friend! Infinite Life Buddha!”

[P49]
“Amen.”

[P50]
Something about that was strange, but Hyeongong didn’t care. He was still beaming when Taekyung continued in his gentle voice.

[P51]
“There is one small problem, though.”

[P52]
“Hm? What problem?”

[P53]
“The corpse is so large that I can’t deal with it alone. And we can’t exactly move it whole.”

[P54]
“Quite right. Quite right.”

[P55]
From head to tail, the creature stretched roughly a hundred zhang.[^1] Whether it could be moved in one piece was doubtful. Doing so would take a great many people, making it impossible to keep the matter secret.

[P56]
“So I’d like to ask you a small favor, Perfected Being.”

[P57]
Hyeongong faltered. Suspicion flickered in his eyes.

[P58]
“Wait, young friend. This favor of yours wouldn’t be…”

[P59]
“Yes. We need you to lend us a hand. At this rate, it’ll take days.”

[P60]
*So that’s it! That’s why he was being so generous!*

[P61]
Hyeongong glared at Taekyung, feeling betrayed.

[P62]
“You want me to use Wudang’s sword arts to take that imugi’s corpse apart?”

[P63]
“Think of it as work.”

[P64]
“Work? You expect me to think of it as work? I did not train in martial arts for this!”

[P65]
Reaching the Supreme Peak realm meant devoting most of one’s life—no, one’s entire life—to martial arts.

[P66]
Hyeongong was no exception. How many years had he spent with a sword as his companion, his beloved? He had even honed his martial arts through secluded meditation, facing a wall in pitch darkness. To him, Taekyung’s request was an insult.

[P67]
*The nerve of him.*

[P68]
His expression hardened.

[P69]
“Infinite Life Buddha. Young friend, you have insulted not only me but the sword arts of the great Wudang Sect.”

[P70]
“Insulted you? I would never. I’m only asking you to lend a hand.”

[P71]
“But I cannot use my sword for something as trivial as—”

[P72]
Just as Hyeongong’s voice began to rise, Taekyung tossed out a remark.

[P73]
“Now that I look at it, your sword’s pretty worn.”

[P74]
“What?”

[P75]
“Seems about time you replaced it. What do you think?”

[P76]
“…!”

[P77]
Hyeongong’s pupils quivered. Before he knew it, he was looking down at the old Pine-Pattern Ancient Sword at his waist.

[P78]
*It certainly is worn… No! What am I thinking?*

[P79]
He had carried that sword since he was ten. It was a precious gift from his late master.

[P80]
Hyeongong shook his head sharply and glared at Taekyung.

[P81]
“It is not worn!”

[P82]
“It is. Look at the hilt. It’s practically falling apart.”

[P83]
“It does seem a little… No! You’re mistaken!”

[P84]
“Fine, forget the hilt. The scabbard’s covered in cracks too. Has it been through a drought?”

[P85]
“Ah! When did those appear…?”

[P86]
“This is worse than I thought. Could you draw the sword?”

[P87]
“Why should I?”

[P88]
*Shing!*

[P89]
Only after shouting did Hyeongong realize he had drawn it. He stared in horror.

[P90]
*When did I do that?*

[P91]
The devil’s whisper went on regardless.

[P92]
“The blade doesn’t look too good either.”

[P93]
“My late master gave me this sword!”

[P94]
Taekyung answered calmly. “My parents gave me this body, but it’s worn down with use. If I could’ve replaced it, I would have done it ages ago.”

[P95]
“Well, this old Daoist’s joints have been aching lately too. I’ve been yearning for Bone Transformation… What are you trying to pull?”

[P96]
“I’m giving you a hard look at reality. Oh, the edge is still sharp.”

[P97]
*Get a grip. Get a grip, Hyeongong.*

[P98]
He steadied his breathing and answered with pride. “Of course it is. The blade was forged with four nyang of Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron mixed into it.”

[P99]
“Good heavens. Four nyang of that precious Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron?”

[P100]
“Do you see now? This sword may look worn, but it is every bit a treasured sword.”

[P101]
“Ah. Is that right?”

[P102]
“Of course! I already own a sword anyone would covet. Why would I need another—”

[P103]
*Clang!*

[P104]
“Oh, sorry. My hand slipped and I dropped my spear. Please, go on.”

[P105]
Hyeongong barely noticed Taekyung’s sheepish smile. His eyes were fixed on the faintly glowing spear, his eyelids trembling.

[P106]
“Y-Young friend. Is that…?”

[P107]
“Nothing special. It’s made of Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron too, but it’s nothing compared to your sword.”

[P108]
It certainly didn’t look that way.

[P109]
Hyeongong swallowed and asked cautiously, “How many nyang?”

[P110]
“Solid. The whole thing, from the blade to the shaft.”

[P111]
“This is fucking insane. Infinite Life Buddha.”

[P112]
“Sorry? What was that?”

[P113]
“Ah, nothing. Nothing at all.”

[P114]
*A devil. This is a devil whispering to me.*

[P115]
Yet as Hyeongong murmured his invocation, his gaze stayed locked on Taekyung’s spear, White Flame.

[P116]
“Light as a feather, incredibly hard, and sharp besides. But…”

[P117]
Then that soft, tempting voice reached his ears again.

[P118]
“I think I’d like a weapon made from an imugi’s bones.”

[P119]
“Infinite Life Buddha. I would not.”

[P120]
“Think about it. A weapon imbued with the qi of a sacred imugi that lived for five hundred years.”

[P121]
*It would be incredible. I want one so badly.*

[P122]
Hyeongong barely swallowed the words and shook his head frantically.

[P123]
“Impossible! I could never abandon the sword my master gave me—”

[P124]
“Who said anything about abandoning it? You can have both.”

[P125]
“Fuck, I could do that! Ah, Primordial Heavenly Venerable!”

[P126]
“Sorry?”

[P127]
“Stop! Enough, young friend! Infinite Life Buddhaa!”

[P128]
“Help us out and we’ll give Wudang a share it can be happy with. You don’t think I’d settle up with a single sword, do you?”

[P129]
“I already have a sword made with Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron!”

[P130]
“Yes. But imugi bones.”

[P131]
“How could I use another sword when I have the one my master gave me?”

[P132]
“Yes. The more, the better.”

[P133]
“I did not learn martial arts for this sort of thing!”

[P134]
Hyeongong clung to his last shred of pride. Taekyung called out past him.

[P135]
“Hey, Young Hero Cheongpung! How’s it going?”

[P136]
A cheerful face popped out from behind the enormous corpse. Cheongpung had been promised a considerable share for fighting alongside them.

[P137]
“Yes, Benefactor! I’m working on the waist!”

[P138]
“Really? That part’s especially thick. Giving you trouble?”

[P139]
“No! The Martial Extremity Grand Unity Sword cuts through it just fine!”

[P140]
“Good. I’ll be there soon. Keep at it.”

[P141]
“Yes, Benefactor!”

[P142]
Taekyung gave the diligent worker a pleased smile, then turned back to Hyeongong.

[P143]
“Ah, forgive me, Perfected Being. I got distracted.”

[P144]
“……”

[P145]
“What were we talking about? I’ve been forgetting things lately.”

[P146]
Hyeongong looked from Cheongpung, hard at work, to Taekyung and back again.

[P147]
Half a shichen later…

[P148]
*Slice!*

[P149]
The Taiji Wisdom Sword, Wudang’s supreme sword technique, was separating the imugi’s scales from its bones.

[P150]
“Murim has gone completely mad.”

[P151]
That was Mungyeong’s brief assessment of everything he had witnessed.

[P152]
[^1]: A zhang is a traditional East Asian unit of length, roughly 3.3 meters.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). **Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.
